## Overview

An end-to-end ML pipeline exploring how socioeconomic indicators — crime rates, education quality, and healthcare access — affect real estate sale prices across Connecticut from 2001 to 2022. Built to answer the question: **beyond location, what actually drives property values?**

---

## Data & Feature Engineering

Data was merged from multiple public sources including Connecticut real estate transaction records, county-level crime statistics, school performance ratings, and hospital access indices.

**Feature engineering steps:**

- Imputation of missing values using median and KNN strategies
- Log transformation of skewed price distributions
- One-hot encoding of categorical variables (town, property type)
- Interaction features between crime rate and school score
- Year-over-year growth rate features

---

## Models

### XGBoost & Random Forest
Ensemble models used for initial benchmarking. XGBoost outperformed Random Forest on RMSE by ~12%, particularly on high-value properties where socioeconomic signals were strongest.

### PyTorch Neural Network
A custom feed-forward network with 4 hidden layers, batch normalization, and dropout regularization. Trained with GPU acceleration and early stopping. Benchmarked against XGBoost — comparable RMSE with significantly higher training cost.

### Production Deployment
- Inference-ready models exported and served via **RESTful APIs**
- Containerized in **Docker** microservice containers
- Automated retraining pipeline triggered on new quarterly data
- Model drift detection monitoring RMSE against rolling baseline

---

## Key Findings

- School quality score had the **strongest positive correlation** with sale price (+0.61)
- Crime rate had a **nonlinear negative effect** — moderate crime showed lower impact than extreme crime
- Healthcare access became a stronger predictor post-2015, suggesting demographic shifts
- Year 2020–2022 showed anomalous price behavior uncapturable by socioeconomic features alone (pandemic effect)
